title: Even This, You'll Miss
author: Ryan Holiday
summary: In this short daily reflection, Ryan Holiday catalogs the exhausting, mundane frustrations of parenting young children — the yelling, tantrums, and endless requests — and argues that even these moments will someday be missed once the house goes quiet and children are grown and gone. He contrasts the eventual calm of an empty house with its loneliness, reminding readers that being needed constantly is a temporary privilege, not a permanent burden. He quotes Laura Ingalls Wilder to argue against wishing the present away, and closes urging parents to ask what they're rushing toward when they find themselves impatient with their kids.
points: Reframes the most exhausting parts of parenting as things that will specifically be missed later, not just endured now.
Uses the concrete image of a future quiet, empty house to make the present chaos feel valuable rather than merely tolerable.
Anchors the reflection in a Laura Ingalls Wilder quote about the irreplaceability of the present moment.
Ends with a practical, actionable prompt — asking what you're rushing toward — rather than just abstract sentiment.
quotes: It's crazy to think, but it's true—someday, even this is something you'll miss.

Right now, you have them. Right now, you're the one they come to with their complaints. Right now, you're the one they ask for stuff. Right now, you're at the center of it. That does not last forever.
Enjoy it while you can. Be present for it while you can. Appreciate it while you can. As loud and obnoxious and infuriating and exhausting as it is…it is a privilege you get for only so long.
'Now is now. It can never be a long time ago,' wrote Laura Ingalls Wilder. Now is all we have. We should never wish a minute of it away.
When you find yourself rushing, ask yourself what you are rushing towards. And remember—someday, you would do anything to get back here to this very moment you are wishing away.
